audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Kings / Melakhim Aleph chapter 13, first-pass draft aligned to public-domain verse structure; formal witness and reception-history audit remains required.
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for altar prophecy, future corpse desecration, temporary hand impairment, healing, prophetic boundaries, deceptive revelation claims, spiritual manipulation, lion death, animal-sign interpretation, mourning, burial, class language, and religious-political critique.

verses.restored: Look, a man of Divine came from Judah by word of YHWH to Bethel, while Jeroboam stood by altar to burn incense.

He cried against altar by word of YHWH: Altar, altar, thus says YHWH: Look, a son shall be born to house of David, Josiah by name. Upon you he shall sacrifice priests of high places who burn incense upon you, and human bones shall be burned upon you.
He gave a sign that day: This is sign YHWH spoke—look, altar shall split and ashes upon it shall be poured out.

When king heard word man of Divine cried against altar in Bethel, Jeroboam stretched his hand from altar, saying, Seize him. His hand which he stretched against him withered/was immobilized, and he could not draw it back to himself.
The altar split and ashes poured from altar according to sign man of Divine gave by word of YHWH.

The king answered man of Divine, Please entreat face of YHWH your Divine and pray for me, that my hand may be restored. Man of Divine entreated face of YHWH, and king's hand was restored and became as before.
The king said to man of Divine, Come home with me and refresh yourself, and I will give you a gift.
Man of Divine said to king, If you give me half your house, I will not go with you, nor eat bread or drink water in this place.
For thus I was commanded by word of YHWH: You shall not eat bread or drink water or return by way you came.
He went by another way and did not return by way he came to Bethel.
An old prophet lived in Bethel. His sons came and recounted to him all work man of Divine did that day in Bethel and words he spoke to king.
Their father said, Which way did he go? His sons had seen way man of Divine from Judah went.
He said to his sons, Saddle donkey for me. They saddled donkey, and he rode upon it.
He went after man of Divine and found him sitting beneath terebinth/oak. He said, Are you man of Divine who came from Judah? He said, I am.
He said to him, Come home with me and eat bread.
He said, I cannot return with you or go with you, nor will I eat bread or drink water with you in this place.
For word came to me by word of YHWH: You shall not eat bread or drink water there or return by way you came.
He said to him, I also am a prophet like you, and a messenger spoke to me by word of YHWH, saying, Bring him back with you to your house so he may eat bread and drink water. But he lied to him.
So he returned with him, ate bread in his house, and drank water.
As they sat at table, word of YHWH came to prophet who brought him back.
He cried to man of Divine who came from Judah: Thus says YHWH: Because you rebelled against mouth of YHWH and did not guard command YHWH your Divine commanded you,
but returned and ate bread and drank water in place of which YHWH said, Eat no bread and drink no water, your corpse shall not come to tomb of your ancestors.
After he ate bread and drank, old prophet saddled donkey for prophet he had brought back.
He went, and a lion met him on road and killed him. His corpse was cast upon road, and donkey stood beside it; lion also stood beside corpse.
Look, people passed and saw corpse cast upon road and lion standing beside corpse. They came and spoke in city where old prophet lived.

Prophet who brought him back heard and said, It is man of Divine who rebelled against mouth of YHWH; therefore YHWH gave him to lion, which broke him and killed him, according to word YHWH spoke to him.
He spoke to his sons, Saddle donkey for me. They saddled it.
He went and found corpse cast upon road, with donkey and lion standing beside corpse. Lion had not eaten corpse or broken donkey.
The prophet lifted corpse of man of Divine, placed it upon donkey, and brought it back. Old prophet came to city to mourn and bury him.
He placed corpse in his own tomb, and they mourned over him: Alas, my brother.
After burying him he said to his sons, When I die, bury me in tomb where man of Divine is buried; place my bones beside his bones.
For word he cried by word of YHWH against altar in Bethel and against all houses of high places in cities of Samaria shall surely come to pass.
After this matter Jeroboam did not turn from his evil way, but again made priests of high places from all the people. Whoever desired, he filled his hand, and the person became priest of high places.
This matter became sin to house of Jeroboam, to cut it off and destroy it from face of earth.

translation_notes: The prophecy anticipates killing priests and burning human bones upon an altar. This is corpse desecration and religious violence, not a model for reform.
Jeroboam's temporary hand impairment is not proof that disabled bodies signify sin. Restoration of movement does not establish his moral innocence either.
The man of Divine states a clear boundary and direct command. The old prophet overrides it by claiming equal prophetic status and an angelic message, while the narrator explicitly says he lied.
This is a foundational spiritual-abuse warning: claims such as 'Divine told me' or 'an angel said' do not erase another person's boundaries, prior discernment, consent, or need for verification.
The deceived man is then condemned and killed. Readers should not turn this disturbing sacred-violence narrative into victim-blaming or obedience terror.
The lion and donkey form an extraordinary literary sign. Animal behavior is not a safe modern divination method, and animals are not props for proving religious authority.
The old prophet's mourning and burial care do not erase his deception or responsibility for drawing the man back.
Verse 33 means priests were made from all the people, not necessarily from a socially 'lowest' class; classist translation should be avoided.
Critique of high places must not authorize persecution, vandalism, or contempt toward contemporary religious minorities.
safety_note: Do not use this chapter to justify killing deceived people, disability stigma, corpse desecration, animal omens, or unquestioning obedience to charismatic revelation claims. Verify claimed messages, protect boundaries, hold deceivers accountable, and preserve grief without blaming the manipulated person.
